text:
ashwin: ran the cross-GPU sweep for max-tokens-per-batch this morning. TL;DR: optimal token ceilings differ a lot by device class, and kernel selection behavior + KV fragmentation are the main regressors. attaching short notes and sample profiles below.

lina: nice, thanks. did you keep runtime kernel selector unchanged?

ashwin: yes, baseline selector unchanged for the first pass. then toggled the new kernel-fit heuristic (fn: kernel_picker=v2) to compare. numbers are median p50/p95 latency for a 32-concurrent-client synthetic mix (seq len mix 8/64/512 ratio 40/40/20).

simon: paste the numbers?

ashwin: sure. summary table (median p50 / p95 in ms) per device class, tokens-per-batch ceiling used in run: 
```
A10  (ceil=2000):  p50=42  p95=128
T4   (ceil=1200):  p50=60  p95=210
L4   (ceil=1800):  p50=48  p95=150
A100 (ceil=8192):  p50=28  p95=95
H100 (ceil=11000): p50=24  p95=85
```
these are with packing enabled and prefix/KV cache warm.

lina: so A100/H100 keep winning as expected. what's the failure mode on T4?

ashwin: T4 shows heavy KV cache fragmentation when mixing short+long: we observed many 1-2 token KV fragments leftover that prevented the long requests from using contiguous KV page regions, leading to more kernel launches and higher p95. Also the kernel_picker=v2 made it worse on T4 because it prefers a tiled-attn kernel that has higher per-launch overhead for short sequences.

perf-bot: regressions detected: kernel_picker=v2 increased p95 by 12% on T4 and 6% on L4 for the same workloads.

eva: interesting. any memory OOMs?

ashwin: no OOMs in these ceilings, but on A10 we hit higher memcpy times for ceilings >2k tokens due to staging buffer growth. So A10 sweetspot around 1800-2200 depending on model width. For L4, 1600-2000 looks stable.

lina: proposal?

ashwin: recommended per-device token_budget_target (for continuous batching) after tuning:
- H100: 10k tokens per batch (ceil=11000) — uses large-kernel path, prefer fused-matmul kernels
- A100: 8k tokens per batch (ceil=8192) — aggressive packing OK
- A10: 2k tokens per batch (ceil=2000) — cap to avoid memcpy stallbacks
- L4: 1.8k tokens per batch (ceil=1800) — guard for kernel-fit overheads
- T4: 1.2k tokens per batch (ceil=1200) — prioritized KV-coalescing + smaller kernel path

Also: set a per-queue policy that enforces two modes: low-latency mode (prefer small-batch flush when p50 budget tight) and high-throughput mode (pack up to the token_budget_target). Mode chosen by route SLO tag.

simon: what about dynamic adjustments based on observed KV fragment ratio?

ashwin: implemented a quick heuristic in the experiment run: if KV_fragment_ratio > 0.25 for >30s, reduce per-device target by 15% and enable coalescing window=20ms to wait for complementary prefixes. That reduced p95 by ~18% on T4 in our replay.

eva: any kernel-selector changes recommended?

ashwin: yes. kernel_picker=v2 should be gated behind a condition: only choose tiled-attn when avg_seq_len > 128 OR when token_budget_target > device_threshold (e.g., >2500). Otherwise prefer the low-launch-overhead kernels. This avoids the overhead for mixed short/long mixes.

lina: sounds reasonable. what about telemetry hooks? we need metrics to guard rollout.

ashwin: suggested metrics:
- token_budget_utilization (per-device, per-queue)
- KV_fragment_ratio (unique kv pages / total kv pages used)
- kernel_launch_count_per_request
- p50/p95 latency by seq_len bucket (8/64/512)
- memcpy_stall_time (ms) per batch

simon: can we add automated rollback if p95 increases >10% after change?

ashwin: yes, rollout plan: canary 5% traffic for 1h, evaluate p95 and KV_fragment_ratio. auto-rollback if p95 delta > +8% OR KV_fragment_ratio increase > +0.1.

eva: does this require a config surface for per-route overrides? many customers will want different SLOs.

ashwin: we already have per-route config for batch_mode and packing hints. just need to expose device_token_budget_target and kernel_picker_overrides with feature flags. I'll draft the config schema after we agree on numbers.

lina: small nit — for A10 we should try 1700 too, staging memcpy times looked variable. can you run a 1700 vs 2000 comparison next run and include memcpy histograms?

ashwin: will do. schedule the run for tonight and post logs.

perf-bot: scheduled bench job 2213456795 for 03:00 UTC. logs will post to #eng-runtime-benchmarks when done. :robot_face:

simon: thanks — this gives us enough to draft a runtime change PR and rollout runbook. once ashwin posts the 1700/2000 A10 comparison we'll pick final numbers.

ashwin: ack, will post results and a short PR checklist tomorrow morning.

lina: great work, folks. :rocket:
